# Wnode Sovereign Compute & Decentralized Wireless (DeWi) Mesh
> Technical Architecture Specification, Execution Invariants, Protocol Schemas, and Lineage Economics Engine

## Executive Overview & System Purpose
Wnode is an autonomous, planetary-scale background compute and decentralized wireless (DeWi) mesh. It orchestrates dormant, idle consumer and enterprise hardware—including off-lease office PCs, spare laptops, homelab servers, mini PCs, and edge micro-routers—into a zero-latency micro-inference and packet routing substrate. 

Unlike legacy DePIN networks that force operators to purchase speculative $600–$2,000 proprietary hardware boxes or mine volatile cryptocurrency tokens, Wnode operates on universal commodity silicon and settles all rewards directly in fiat USD via Stripe Connect. Workloads are strictly ephemeral, executing in volatile RAM sandboxes with zero persistent storage writes, zero disk degradation, and zero GPU thermal stress.

---

## 1. Native Sandboxing & Memory Isolation Invariants

### 1.1 Native Daemon (`nodld`) Architecture
The Wnode node daemon (`nodld`) is built as a zero-dependency, statically linked Go binary running across macOS (Darwin arm64/amd64), Linux (x86_64/arm64), and Windows (x64). It executes with unprivileged user rights (`nobody` / limited process token) and interfaces directly with localized WebAssembly (Wasm) runtimes.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        Host System (PC / Laptop)                   |
|                                                                   |
|  +-------------------------------------------------------------+  |
|  |                 Wnode Daemon (`nodld`)                      |  |
|  |  - Telemetry Ping & Health Engine                           |  |
|  |  - Cryptographic Signature Verifier (Ed25519)                |  |
|  |  - Ephemeral RAM Allocator                                  |  |
|  +------------------------------+------------------------------+  |
|                                 |                                 |
|                                 v                                 |
|  +-------------------------------------------------------------+  |
|  |               wazero WebAssembly RAM Sandbox                |  |
|  |  - Memory Boundary: Ring 3 / No Host Syscalls               |  |
|  |  - Ephemeral Heap: Cleared on Job Completion                |  |
|  |  - I/O Isolation: No Disk Access (Zero SSD TBW Wear)       |  |
|  +-------------------------------------------------------------+  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 1.2 Isolation Guarantees & Memory Security
- **Runtime Sandboxing**: Micro-inference workloads run inside `wazero`, a pure-Go, zero-CGO WebAssembly compiler and interpreter. Sandboxed guest execution cannot invoke host syscalls (`execve`, `open`, `mmap`, `socket`) or inspect host filesystem structures.
- **Zero Disk Retention (SSD Protection)**: All binary payload assets, model weights slice buffers, and intermediate tensor activation maps are streamed into memory buffers. Output tokens are streamed back via TLS 1.3 WebSockets. Upon job completion or eviction, memory region pointers are zeroized and released via `runtime.GC()`. No scratch files, temp directories, or cache blocks touch the host storage media.
- **Dynamic Bounded Allocation**: The operator defines hard caps (e.g., max 4GB RAM, 50% CPU allocation) via configuration flags. `nodld` uses cgroups v2 (Linux) or `JobObjects` (Windows) to strictly enforce process memory boundaries, preventing host OOM (Out Of Memory) events.

---

## 2. Memory Wall Mitigation & Test-Time Inference Distribution

### 2.1 The Memory Wall Problem in LLM Inference
Large Language Model (LLM) inference—specifically autoregressive transformer generation—is bound by memory bandwidth rather than raw FLOP count. Loading multi-billion parameter FP16/INT8 weight matrices into memory per token generation creates a bottleneck on monolithic cloud GPUs.

### 2.2 KV Cache Sharding & Test-Time Compute Distribution
Wnode addresses the Memory Wall through distributed tensor slice execution and KV Cache sharding across consumer RAM channels:

```
[Inference Request] --> [Wnode Gateway Router]
                             |
         +-------------------+-------------------+
         |                   |                   |
         v                   v                   v
  +--------------+    +--------------+    +--------------+
  | Node A (RAM) |    | Node B (RAM) |    | Node C (RAM) |
  | KV Cache #1  |    | KV Cache #2  |    | KV Cache #3  |
  +-------+------+    +-------+------+    +-------+------+
          |                   |                   |
          +-------------------+-------------------+
                             |
                             v
               [Aggregated Output Stream]
```

1. **Layer-Wise Weight Partitioning**: Models are split across participating nodes based on available RAM. Node A holds Layers 0–11, Node B holds Layers 12–23, Node C holds Layers 24–35.
2. **Key-Value (KV) Cache Streaming**: During test-time reasoning and chain-of-thought generation, intermediate KV tensors are streamed via high-speed peer-to-peer WebSocket meshes with LZ4 compression.
3. **Consumer Dual-Channel RAM Throughput**: Modern DDR4/DDR5 dual-channel memory systems provide 50–100 GB/s bandwidth. Aggregating 1,000 idle desktop nodes creates terabytes of volatile high-speed memory capable of serving massive context windows without expensive data center H100 GPUs.

---

## 3. Circular Eco-Compute vs. Hyperscale Data Center Environmental Impact

### 3.1 Data Center Water Crisis & Power Grid Strain
Hyperscale AI data centers consume gigawatts of electricity and millions of gallons of potable water daily for evaporative cooling towers. This places severe thermal stress on local power grids and depletes regional water tables.

### 3.2 Wnode Zero-Water & Zero-Concrete Framework
- **Decentralized Air Cooling**: Consumer PCs, laptops, and homelab servers rely on existing passive ambient air cooling. Wnode redistributes inference tasks globally, keeping individual node CPU temperatures well within standard operational thresholds (under 60°C).
- **Zero Additional Civil Infrastructure**: Wnode requires no new concrete data center construction, high-voltage transformers, or industrial chiller plants. It operates entirely on already-manufactured, powered-on, and underutilized dormant silicon.
- **E-Waste Upcycling**: Off-lease office PCs (e.g., Dell OptiPlex, HP EliteDesk) and older laptops discarded by corporations are repurposed into productive revenue-generating compute nodes, extending hardware lifespans by 5–10 years.

## 4. Web3 Unification Layer & 600+ Protocol Intent Substrate

### 4.1 Cross-Chain Execution Substrate
Wnode acts as a stateless, neutral execution engine for decentralized applications, autonomous AI agents, MEV searchers, and cross-chain intent solvers.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  Wnode Web3 Unification Engine                    |
|                                                                   |
|  +--------------------+  +------------------+  +---------------+  |
|  | EVM RPC Fabric     |  | SVM Intent Engine|  | Cosmos IBC    |  |
|  | (Ethereum/Arbitrum)|  | (Solana/Eclipse) |  | Relayer Core  |  |
|  +---------+----------+  +--------+---------+  +-------+-------+  |
|            |                      |                    |          |
|            +----------------------+--------------------+          |
|                                   |                               |
|                                   v                               |
|  +-------------------------------------------------------------+  |
|  |            600+ Protocol Automation Hooks                   |  |
|  |  - Decentralized Oracle Verification                        |  |
|  |  - Stateless Proof Generation (ZK-SNARK/STARK)             |  |
|  |  - Cross-Chain Liquidity Routing                            |  |
|  +-------------------------------------------------------------+  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 4.2 Supported Protocol Categories & Capabilities
- **Universal RPC Aggregation**: Pooled, latency-routed RPC endpoints covering 600+ EVM, SVM, and Move networks with automatic fallback and state sanitization.
- **Stateless Zero-Knowledge Proofs**: Offloading heavy ZK-SNARK and ZK-STARK circuit compilation to idle desktop CPU workers.
- **DeWi & Packet Relaying**: Off-grid LoRa, Helium, and Reticulum packet verification, allowing micro-ISPs to route telemetry without exposing public IP addresses.

## 5. Stripe Connect Fiat Settlements & Bounded Two-Tier Lineage Economics

### 5.1 Direct Rev-Share Allocation Breakdown
Wnode eliminates speculative crypto tokenomics, gas fee volatility, and DEX slippage by settling all rewards in fiat USD.

```
Gross Compute Job Revenue ($100.00)
 ├── 70% ($70.00) Direct Node Operator Yield (via Stripe Connect)
 ├── 10% ($10.00) Lifetime Sales Source Commission (Customer Acquirer)
 ├── 10% ($10.00) Wnode Platform Infrastructure & Mesh Maintenance
 └── 10% ($10.00) Referral Override Reserve
      ├── 3% ($3.00) Level 1 Direct Referral Override
      └── 7% ($7.00) Level 2 Extended Network Override
```

### 5.2 Stripe Connect Batching & Ledger Invariants
- **Minimum Payout Floor**: To prevent microscopic bank fee friction, payouts are batched and transferred once an operator's ledger balance reaches **$25.00 USD**.
- **Automated ACH & Debit Distributions**: Operators connect their bank account or debit card via Stripe Connect onboarding. Funds transfer automatically on a weekly or threshold-triggered cadence.
- **Cryptographic Lineage Ledger**: Node referral lineage is recorded using immutable SHA-256 HMAC parent chains. Referral overrides are capped at strictly two tiers (L1 3%, L2 7%), enforcing non-MLM legal compliance and mathematical solvency.
